approachQuestion.prompt:
Cancel a Known Queue Entry

A finite acyclic doubly linked list has correct reciprocal prev/next links, head.prev=null and tail.next=null. You receive head, tail and a direct reference victim guaranteed to be one of its nodes. Remove victim, preserve all other node identities, values and order, clear victim.prev and victim.next, and return the new head and tail. Nodes need not be freed. You may change links but not values. Constraints: 1 <= n <= 200000; no search for victim is required.

Input: A <-> B <-> C, victim=B. Output: head A, tail C, A <-> C, and B.prev=B.next=null.
Input: single A, victim=A. Output: head=null, tail=null, with A detached.

Choose a method that satisfies the full contract with the best worst-case running time, breaking time ties by least auxiliary storage.

options.text: Copy the successor's value into victim and unlink that successor.
options.feedback: For A(1) <-> B(2), victim=A, the survivor must be object B with value 2, not object A. A tail victim has no successor.

options.text: Save victim.prev and victim.next. Link the predecessor to the successor when it exists, otherwise update head. Link the successor back to the predecessor when it exists, otherwise update tail. Clear both victim links.
options.feedback: The supplied neighboring links identify every affected boundary, including removing the only node.

options.text: Walk from head to locate victim and its neighbors, then perform the same boundary updates and clearing.
options.feedback: This is correct, but searches for a node whose location and neighbors were already supplied.

options.text: Only assign victim.prev.next=victim.next without checking boundaries or updating any other links.
options.feedback: Removing head dereferences null; removing an interior node also leaves successor.prev pointing to victim.

complexityQuestion.prompt: Analyze only the revealed method (acm-b15-15-target), regardless of your Q1 choice. Here n. Choose the tight worst-case time and auxiliary-space pair.
constraints: Count each node allocation, link access, identity/value comparison and machine-word operation as constant work. Include all temporary collections and call frames; exclude supplied nodes and the final returned output only. Copying or allocating k records costs k operations. No hash-table, amortized-operation or tail-call assumptions are used.
